Not relevant - given as an intravenous infusion

summary: Cetuximab is a chimeric anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody used to treat KRAS wild-type (RAS wild-type), EGFR-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer and squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. It carries a BOXED WARNING for serious, sometimes fatal infusion reactions (including anaphylaxis) and for cardiopulmonary arrest and sudden death, particularly when combined with radiation or platinum-based therapy in head and neck cancer. The standard schedule is an initial loading dose of 400 mg/m2 followed by weekly 250 mg/m2, or a biweekly 500 mg/m2 regimen. It must NOT be used for RAS-mutant colorectal cancer because there is no benefit and potential harm. Other key risks include pulmonary toxicity (interstitial lung disease), severe dermatologic toxicity (acneiform rash, infections), and hypomagnesaemia with related electrolyte disturbances. Premedication with an antihistamine and close monitoring during and after infusion are required.
indications: KRAS wild-type (RAS wild-type), EGFR-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer, in combination with FOLFIRI or irinotecan, or as a single agent after prior chemotherapy
Locally or regionally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck in combination with radiation therapy
Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck in combination with platinum-based therapy and fluorouracil, or as a single agent after prior platinum-based therapy

dosage.t: IV infusion over 120 minutes (max rate 10 mg/min)
dosage.n: Premedicate with an H1 antihistamine; complete the loading dose 1 week before starting radiation in head/neck regimens

dosage.t: IV infusion over 60 minutes (max rate 10 mg/min)
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.d: Reduce infusion rate or interrupt for reactions; reduce/withhold for severe acneiform rash; discontinue for severe (grade 3-4) infusion reaction or interstitial lung disease
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue for serious infusion reaction or pulmonary toxicity

admin: Confirm RAS (KRAS/NRAS) wild-type status before use in colorectal cancer - do NOT use in RAS-mutant tumours
Premedicate with an H1 antihistamine (e.g. diphenhydramine); corticosteroid premedication may be added per protocol
Give the initial dose over 120 minutes and subsequent doses over 60 minutes; do not exceed an infusion rate of 10 mg/min
Monitor closely during and for at least 1 hour after each infusion; have resuscitation equipment and medication available
Administer through an in-line filter; do not give as an IV push or bolus and do not shake the vial
Monitor and replete serum magnesium, calcium and potassium during and after treatment
moa: Cetuximab is a recombinant chimeric (human/mouse) IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the extracellular domain of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) with higher affinity than its natural ligands. This blocks ligand binding and receptor dimerisation, inhibiting EGFR autophosphorylation and downstream signalling pathways (RAS-RAF-MAPK and PI3K-AKT) that drive proliferation, survival, angiogenesis and metastasis. It also promotes receptor internalisation/downregulation and, as an IgG1 antibody, can recruit antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. Tumours with activating downstream RAS mutations are resistant because signalling proceeds independently of EGFR.

absolute: RAS-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (no benefit and potential harm)
relative: Pre-existing cardiopulmonary disease (higher risk of cardiopulmonary arrest, especially with radiation/platinum)
monitor: Infusion reactions during and after the first and subsequent infusions
Cardiac and pulmonary status, especially with radiation/platinum
Serum magnesium, calcium and potassium during and for weeks after treatment
Skin for severe acneiform rash and secondary infection

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal data, cetuximab can cause fetal harm, including embryo-fetal toxicity. It should not be used in pregnancy. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for a period (e.g. about 2 months) after the last dose.
lact: It is not known whether cetuximab is excreted in human milk, but human IgG is. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant, women should not breastfeed during treatment and for about 2 months after the final dose.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is recommended for renal impairment. Cetuximab can cause hypomagnesaemia and associated electrolyte disturbances, so renal handling of magnesium and electrolytes should be monitored and corrected.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment for hepatic impairment has been established; monitor patients clinically.

major: Radiation therapy and platinum-based chemotherapy - increased risk of serious cardiopulmonary events including sudden death (boxed warning)
Other potentially cardiotoxic or QT-affecting agents - additive cardiac risk
moderate: Concurrent chemotherapy (irinotecan, fluorouracil, platinum) - additive toxicity such as diarrhoea, mucositis and myelosuppression
minor: As a monoclonal antibody, classic CYP-mediated drug interactions are not expected
interactions.alcohol: No direct interaction; moderation advised during cancer therapy
interactions.diagnostics: Requires tumour RAS (KRAS/NRAS) and EGFR testing before use; can lower serum magnesium, calcium and potassium on laboratory testing

common: Acneiform skin rash, dry skin, pruritus and nail changes (paronychia)
serious: Severe, sometimes fatal infusion reactions including anaphylaxis (boxed warning)
Cardiopulmonary arrest and sudden death, especially with radiation/platinum therapy (boxed warning)
Severe dermatologic toxicity with secondary skin infection/sepsis
Severe hypomagnesaemia with hypocalcaemia/hypokalaemia and arrhythmia risk
emergency: Cardiopulmonary arrest or acute cardiac event

monitoring: Vital signs and reaction monitoring during and for at least 1 hour after each infusion
Serum magnesium, calcium and potassium periodically during and for up to 8 weeks after completing therapy
Skin assessment for acneiform rash and secondary infection
Respiratory symptoms suggestive of interstitial lung disease
Cardiac status, particularly with concurrent radiation or platinum chemotherapy
counsel: This is an antibody given by a drip to treat your cancer; reactions can occur during or shortly after the infusion - tell staff immediately of breathlessness, dizziness, chest tightness, fever or rash
An acne-like rash and dry, sensitive skin are common - use moisturiser, sun protection, and report severe or infected rash
Protect your skin from the sun, as the rash can worsen with sun exposure
Report tingling, muscle cramps or palpitations, which may indicate low magnesium
Use effective contraception during treatment and for about 2 months afterwards, and do not breastfeed
Keep all appointments for blood tests, including magnesium and electrolyte checks
pk: EGFR blockade begins with the first infusion
Serum concentrations peak at the end of the infusion
Elimination half-life approximately 5 days (around 70-100 hours); steady state reached after about 3 weeks of weekly dosing
Sustained EGFR inhibition supports weekly or biweekly dosing
Store vials refrigerated at 2-8 C; do not freeze or shake; protect from light per label
pearls: BOXED WARNING: serious/fatal infusion reactions (including anaphylaxis) and cardiopulmonary arrest/sudden death, especially with radiation or platinum-based therapy in head/neck cancer
Use only in RAS (KRAS/NRAS) wild-type, EGFR-expressing colorectal cancer - it is harmful/ineffective in RAS-mutant tumours, so test first
Premedicate with an antihistamine and monitor for at least 1 hour after each infusion
Hypomagnesaemia is common - monitor and replete magnesium, calcium and potassium during and after therapy
Acneiform rash is expected and may correlate with response; severe rash and interstitial lung disease require dose modification or discontinuation
missed: Cetuximab is administered by a healthcare professional on a fixed schedule. If an appointment is missed, the oncology team will reschedule the infusion; do not attempt to adjust dosing yourself.
overdose: There is no established antidote and limited data on overdose; the maximum tolerated single dose has not been determined. Management is supportive with intensified monitoring for infusion reactions, cardiopulmonary events, dermatologic toxicity and electrolyte disturbances, treating each as it arises.
